purpose: personal account of why Alexey began researching the still-forming AI Engineer role

required_facts.fact: AI Engineer and Gen AI Engineer titles had become more common on job boards, LinkedIn, and community discussions, while the role lacked a stable definition.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 1-6: title growth, role ambiguity, and inconsistent expectations are stated.

required_facts.fact: As the AI Engineering Buildcamp instructor, Alexey found the role relevant to course participants and hiring questions.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 16: course context and relevance are described.

required_facts.fact: A participant asked during Office Hours for concrete examples of AI Engineer take-home interview assignments.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 16: the practical question is stated.

required_facts.fact: Alexey had more than 15 years of ML and AI experience but was not currently employed as an AI Engineer.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 18 and 30: experience and current employment qualification are given.

required_facts.fact: He began collecting actual data rather than relying only on indirect exposure or conversations.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 18: the research motivation is stated.

required_facts.fact: The research combined personal experience, structured data collection, and practitioner conversations.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 20 and 24: research signals and the three-part input plan are described.

required_facts.fact: More than 1,500 job postings from three months across cities including Los Angeles, New York, London, Amsterdam, and Berlin were collected.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 39: dataset size, period, and locations are stated.

required_facts.fact: Twitter/X and Reddit interview discussions were used to capture informal, recent patterns.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 52-59: social sources and their purpose are described.

required_facts.fact: Planned conversations included hiring managers, DataTalks.Club members, and engineers working in AI Engineering roles.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 61-74: conversation groups and privacy/publicity are specified.

required_facts.fact: Around 60 public GitHub repositories with take-home solutions were collected, with manual review needed because research agents hallucinated or missed requested results.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 78-89: repository dataset and hybrid collection workflow are described.

author_attribution: Attribute the research motivation, uncertainty, and data-collection choices to Alexey; preserve that the role remained evolving rather than defined.
